deities: No enshrined deities - this is a sacred natural hill, not a temple. The Khasi indigenous faith centres on U Blei Nongthaw (God the Creator), honoured at the summit by Seng Khasi devotees (verify details)
festivals: Annual Seng Khasi pilgrimage on the first Sunday of February (several sources) - the official Meghalaya tourism site says the second Sunday of February (verify which Sunday), with rites, rituals, traditional dances and songs on the summit
Renewal-of-traditions rites: devotees climb the peak to acknowledge their legends and pledge to keep their unique traditions alive

history.summary: IMPORTANT: Lum Sohpetbneng is NOT a Hindu temple. It is the most sacred natural site of the Khasi people, practitioners of the indigenous Niam Khasi religion. 'Sohpetbneng' means 'navel of heaven'. Central Khasi cosmology holds that a golden vine bridge or ladder (Jingkieng Ksiar) once connected heaven and earth at this peak, down which 16 celestial families descended to earth; seven of them chose to stay and became the ancestors of the Khasi people (the Hynniewtrep, 'Seven Huts' people of the West Khasi, East Khasi, Ri-Bhoi and Jaintia Hills). According to divine decree, the bridge was severed because of human pride and sin. The Seng Khasi organisation holds annual prayers and rituals on the summit, and thousands climb the hill each February for the pilgrimage. The peak stands about 1,343 m (some sources say 1,344 m - verify) on the Guwahati-Shillong highway adjacent to Umiam Lake, with a tall gateway featuring traditional motifs at its base and panoramic views of Shillong's outskirts and the lake from the top. CSV town 'Mairang' is WRONG - the site is in Ri-Bhoi district, nowhere near Mairang (which is in the Eastern West Khasi Hills, on the Shillong-Nongstoin road).

name: Lum Sohpetbneng
town: Near Umiam Lake (CSV town 'Mairang' is incorrect - the peak is in Ri-Bhoi district, not Mairang)
town_description: The peak lies on the Guwahati-Shillong highway adjacent to Umiam Lake (Barapani) in Ri-Bhoi district, about 25 km from Shillong and 15-17 km from the lake area, with Nongpoh (the Ri-Bhoi district headquarters) to the north. Ri-Bhoi is the gateway district of Meghalaya from Assam, known for Umiam Lake, the Orchid Lake Resort and waterfalls. Mairang, named in the CSV, is a town in the Eastern West Khasi Hills on the Shillong-Nongstoin road, roughly 40 km west of Shillong in the opposite direction - it has no connection to this site (verify distance).

travel.airport: Shillong Airport (approx. 15 km); Guwahati Airport (approx. 107 km) - distances per Meghalaya Tourism
travel.railway: Guwahati Railway Station (approx. 84 km) - per Meghalaya Tourism
travel.road: Base of the hill is on the Guwahati-Shillong highway near Umiam Lake, marked by a tall gateway with traditional motifs; hire a local taxi from Shillong. The summit is reached by a gentle climb (about 1.5 hours on foot per some accounts - verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. February (first or second Sunday - verify) for the annual Seng Khasi pilgrimage, which draws large crowds; day visits are otherwise recommended.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Free entry, no entry fee. One travel listing gives daily 6:00 AM to 5:00 PM (verify - confirm locally; day visits recommended by Meghalaya Tourism).
